test: PicoCalc STM32F103 RTC second-event cache: real board control then final fixed candidate
implementation: Poll latched SECF instead of two HAL calls per foreground turn; no additional IRQ or STOP wakeup
Retain real F1 HAL calendar rollover; invalidate after startup, both I2C setters and calendar restore
W0C-safe SECF acknowledgement preserves alarm/overflow/synchronization flags and CNF
Publish date/time together only when generation unchanged and no new second arrived
SECF precedes CNT by one RTCCLK; keep pending if snapshot has not advanced, retry next main turn without busy-wait
HAL errors leave refresh pending; previous interrupt mask restored

sequence: detect persistent one-second lag in full logs
fix and reproduce early-SECF regression offline
method.native_case_order: 0,1,2 on even repetitions; 2,1,0 on odd repetitions
method.native_timer: Actual M3 API microsecond timer; whole cooperative job spans BIOS foreground services
method.AY_timer: Pico microsecond timer including UART exchange; separate M3 render timer
method.checksums: Independent host LCG results and AY PCM vectors; equal across all measured firmware
method.comparison_limit: Control measured on 18 November, final candidate on 19 November at the same Pico image/clocks. No return to control; ambient conditions not controlled. Ranges describe repeated runs, not a randomized confidence interval. Not whole-program FPS or streaming PWM audio.

clock_validation.scope: Clock read-only on board; setters, leap/year/midnight and STOP-sized jumps exercised in HOST/ARM models.
